question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/37674375730f32a70d7909a7ab01f3f9c836cf9c72d16447d499af20427f022c.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1)$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>-a)=P(Z<a)=Φ(a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z>-2.28).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/8de2f1c38c81136c0d0ab7471e9a1c90d2b55da37593c235e2c227baf67473d9.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z<2.28).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/54fec3abcac7bdbd3b03317af790350f5d908a346bb81a3ae584710998210543.png)

Therefore,

$$
P(Z>-2.28)=P(Z<2.28)=Φ(2.28)=0.9887.
$$
